st.t: Global Network of BAPS - Hari Mandirs - Ashton-U-Lvne
w: History First Satsang was started in Ashton by Durgeshbhai Dave in 1971, when he made Kishorebhai Desai’s family satsangi and both decided to do satsang weekly.

1971 17th August the first weekly sabha was started on every Saturday at Kishorebhai’s residence - 66 Princes street. In that sabha, Thakorbhai’s family, Bakulbhai, Mukeshbhai, Rajendrabhai, Bhupendrabhai, Maganbhai Patel’s family, Harshadbhai (P. Chinmaiswami), Mukehsbhai, Dineshbhai, Vijaybhai Patel’s family, Gopalbhai’s family, Kantibhai Patel’s family, Mohanbhai Patel’s family, Vikrambhai Patel’s family, Rameshbhai’s family, Jagidishbhai Brahmbhatt’s family, etc. started to come for Satsang.
1972 Maharaj’s Janmajayanti was celebrated at Hurst Cross Community Hall. Prafulbhai Patel, Dr. Swaminarayan, P. C. Patel and Yuvaks came from London to attend this celebrations.
1972 Kishorebhai Desai, Naginbhai Mistri, Kantibhai Patel and Thakorbhai went to India to participate with P. P. Swamishri in Special Train Trip for India.

1974 P. P. Swamishri came to U K and visited Ashton. Sabha was at Dunkinfield Town Hall, Hurst Cross Community Hall and Bharatiya Mandal. Swamishri’s accommodation was at Thakorbhai’s residence. The meeting was held between Swamishri and Haribhaktos. In that it was decided to buy the house of Balubhai and Gopalbhai for Satsang kendra.
1975 As the mandir in Cowhill was ready, On Akha Trij Murti were shifted their. The first pujari was Kantibhai Patel.
1977 P. P. Swamishri came to U K. During that visit he came to Ashton and huge procession took place. After that, Murti’s were consecrated by Swamishri.
1980 P. P. Swamishri came to U K. In that time one old factory was borrowed at 29 Russell Street which was converted to Hari Mandir after some alteration and renovations.
1985 P. P. Swamishri visited Ashton during U K visit. Nitin Patel went to India for Sadhu’s diksha. (P. Vimaljivanswami)

1994 P. P. Swamishri visited Ashton during his visit to U K. Huge procession of marble Murti’s took place in city. The first Marble Murti’s were consecrated by P. P. Swamishri in U K at Ashton after that procession.
In the evening assembly Lord Harikrishna Maharaj was honored by the devotees.

st.t: Shri Nilkanth Varni Murti Pratishtha and First Anniversary Celebrations at BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Houston -August 14, 2005 USA
w: Devotees from all around the nation gathered at the BAPS Shree Swaminarayan Mandir, Houston to celebrate the first anniversary of the first traditional Mandir in North America. Celebrations commenced on Saturday, August 13th and continued through August 14th. The highlights of this two day event were Shri Nilkanth Varni murti pratistha and opening of Pramukh Dwar on Sunday morning, a colorful nagar yatra involving men and women of all ages on Saturday evening and a brilliant fireworks display synchronized with music on Saturday night.

Saturday's festivities started with a nagar yatra of Thakorji and Shri Nilkanth Varni around the mandir campus. The murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni was pulled in a magnificent rath created to look like the Himalayan Mountains as Bal/Balikas dressed in traditional costumes, performed dance along the route. The band from Dallas lead the nagar yatra adding rhythm and enthusiasm to the whole event. Everyone participating or watching the nagar yatra immensely enjoyed the festivities. The celebration climaxed Saturday night with a breathtaking show of fireworks.

Sunday morning marked another day of celebration including the murti pratishtha of the Shri Nilkanth Varni's murti and the opening of Pramukh Dwar. The intricately carved Gate stands as a magnificent entrance to the Mandir. Structured in a traditional fashion with delicate statues and statuettes adorned with various symbols to wholeheartedly welcome all who come to visit God. Congressman Nick Lampson, Honorable Deputy Consul General of India K.P. Pillai, and Houston city council member Gordon Quan performed the Gate opening ceremony on Sunday morning. Speaking after the ceremony, Congressman Nick Lampson expressed his amazement at the grandeur of the Mandir and the experience it brings. All dignitaries in attendance were amazed at the sight of the Mandir and Gate and enjoyed their visit.

Following this event was the Shri Nilkanth Varni murti Pratishtha . Pujya Yagnavallabh Swami joined by other santos, consecrated the murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni. As a mark of devotion and gratitude to Shri Nilkanth Varni's sacrifice and compassion for humanity, devotees will daily offer abhishek to the murti of Nilkanth Varni by bathing the sacred image with sanctified water. Following the murti Pratishtha , there was a short sabha, during which BAPS honored the new Deputy Consul General of India, K. P. Pillai.

His Divine Holiness Pramukh Swami Maharaj blessed the festivities via a live conference call. He blessed everyone for good health, prosperity, happiness, and faith in God. Everyone present recalled the previous year when Swamishri opened the Mandir. The various events of the weekend were a grand and ideal way to celebrate the first anniversary of the Mandir and also to welcome the murti of Nilkanth Varni. The festivities provided the seamless blend of reminiscence and hope for the future.

After the flood waters started subsiding, Swamishri instructed the senior sadhus of Surat mandir to take up a cleaning-up project in one of the suburbs as requested by the state government. He advised that more BAPS youth volunteers be called from our centres in Navsari, Valsad and Sankari. Swamishri further instructed that the cleaning-up work was to be done in collaboration with government officials, and the Sanstha’s medical vans be deployed in the city. As part of flood relief services, Swamishri instructed the BAPS mandirs in Amdavad, Mumbai, Bochasan, Atladra, etc. The 50-75 kg kit included wheat floor, grains, spices, ghee, edible oil, etc.

The evening celebration assembly was interlaced with speeches and dance. Aksharvatsal Swami, Viveksagar Swami and Tyagvallabh Swami spoke about the divine life of Bhagwan Shri Krishna. BAPS teenagers performed a lively traditional dance based on the bhajan “Govinda ãlã re…”, describing Krishna’s pastime as a child. Thereafter Swamishri was honoured with garlands. Finally at 9.40 p.m. Swamishri blessed the assembly, “We celebrate such festivals because of our devotion to God, to please him, to experience his divine bliss and to attain his divine abode. To listen and remember his divine incidents is also a means to attain moksha. When we attain God and his realized Sadhu we experience inner peace. Material things or pleasures do not provide inner peace, but cause turmoil.”Swamishri concluded his blessings at 10.00 p.m. Thereafter he devotionally rocked Thakorji in a decorated hindolo amidst the singing of “Nand gher ãnand bhayo… ”.

A youth who was a spiritual seeker came for darshan. He said, "I have an intense desire to become a sadhu, but as soon as my mother and father came to know of this, they got me married. Please use your power to change things, so that I can explain to the girl and separate from her, and then I can become a sadhu."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "There is no need to do anything like that. Please your mother and father. Stay there and do the seva of satsang."
At the end of his walk, Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat on his bed to rest. Then Bhagwatcharan Swami, standing in front of him, said, "You have great happiness!"

In a joyful mood Swamishri said, "We have attained God, we have attained Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. Where in this world is there any happiness greater than this? If this is believed, then whether we fall ill or are well, whether someone speaks against us, insults us or honours us, there will be only happiness, happiness and happiness."

A young seeker came for darshan. He said, "I have an intense desire to become a sadhu, but as soon as my mother and father came to know of it, they got me married. Please use your power to change things, and let me explain to the girl and separate from her, so that I can become a sadhu."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "There is no need to do anything like that. Please your parents. Stay there and do seva for satsang."
At the end of his walk, Pramukh Swami Maharaj sat on his bed to go and rest. Then Bhagwatcharan Swami, standing in front, said, "You are so very happy!"

In high spirits, Swamishri said, "We have found Bhagwan, we have found Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj, where in this world is there greater happiness than that? If this is believed, then whether we fall ill or are healthy, whether someone speaks ill of us, insults us or honours us, there remains happiness, happiness and only happiness."

After giving puja darshan, as Mahant Swami Maharaj entered the passage of the sadhus' ashram, he stopped on seeing a photo of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Pramukh Swami Maharaj's right index finger is on his lips, and his eyes look as if he is looking straight at us, thinking something. Swamishri is a complete expert at reading feelings! So he immediately turned back to the sadhus and asked, "What is Bapa thinking?"
Brahmvatsaldas Swami said, "Please tell us yourself..."
Brahmviharidas Swami said, "Only you can tell..."
Swamishri burst out laughing and said, "He wants to make everyone brahmarup."
The sadhus clapped and swayed with joy, because through his guru, Swamishri himself had told us, "He wants to make everyone brahmarup!"
This evening Mahant Swami Maharaj came to the Kishore Day assembly. In one programme, Swamishri had to choose the answers to questions from given options.
Question 1: "What is the means to moksha?"
Swamishri ticked "The great sadhu."
Question 2: "What is the meaning of firm love?"
Swamishri chose the option "To do whatever pleases the great sadhu."
Question 3: "Which divine action of Pramukh Swami Maharaj do you like?"
Swamishri answered, "Laughing."

After that, so that they would remember Swamishri whenever they used their phones, Swamishri was requested to send them all a text message with his message. Swamishri sent the message: "Divyabhav (seeing divinity)." As planned, in the blink of an eye it reached everyone's mobile.
Finally, Swamishri was asked, "What is one thing that reminds you of Pramukh Swami Maharaj?"
After thinking for a while, Swamishri said, "Bapa's shoes."
When Swamishri came to his room, the sadhus asked, "As the thing that reminds you of Bapa, you said 'Bapa's shoes.' Why shoes?"
Swamishri said, "When Bapa walked, his heels would drag and the soles would wear down. That brings back his memory."
Munichintandas Swami lifted his own foot and began showing the heel, asking, "It wore down here, didn't it?"
Swamishri said, "Not on one foot, on both feet."
Because the attendant sadhu had naturally been showing it by lifting just one foot. But what subtle vision! What detailed memory! How much love there must be for such a memory to come!!
